name: Oregon

code.name: Oregon Revised Statutes
code.edition: ORS 2025 Edition, as the Oregon Legislature's chapter pages print it (chapter 254, Conduct of Elections, and chapter 258, Election Contests; Recounts, each headed '2025 EDITION')

or-254.citation: ORS chapter 254 (Conduct of Elections), 2025 Edition: 254.005 (definitions, chief elections officer), 254.575 (procedure when tie vote)

or-258.citation: ORS chapter 258 (Election Contests; Recounts), 2025 Edition: 258.161 (demand for recount), 258.250 (payment of cost of recount), 258.280 (automatic full recount, candidates), 258.290 (automatic full recount, measures)

ties.applies_to: election to state Senator or Representative, a party office, or a public office for which the elections officer is other than the Secretary of State (county, city and district offices), where two or more candidates for the same office, after a full recount of votes, have an equal and the highest number of votes (ORS 254.575(1))
ties.steps: a full recount is made first (it is ordered automatically on a tie, ORS 258.280(1)(a)); if the candidates are still tied the elections officer has them meet publicly to decide by lot who is elected
ties.who: the elections officer (the Secretary of State's office does not decide these; for county offices the county clerk)

sources.quote: When two or more candidates for the same office, after a full recount of votes, have an equal and the highest number of votes: [...] (1) For election to state Senator or Representative, a party office, or a public office for which the elections officer is other than the Secretary of State, the elections officer shall have the candidates meet publicly to decide by lot who is elected.
(a) Two or more candidates for that nomination or office have an equal and the highest number of votes; or

ties.note: Local offices are read as 'a public office for which the elections officer is other than the Secretary of State' because ORS 254.005 makes the county clerk the chief elections officer for a county office and the Secretary of State only for a state office, an office voted in the state at large or in a congressional district [inferred]; city and district offices and home rule charters were not read.

ties.applies_to: election to a public office other than Governor and other than those in subsection (1): U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, presidential electors, and other statewide offices, after a full recount (ORS 254.575(2))
ties.steps: a full recount is made first; if the candidates are still tied the Secretary of State by proclamation orders a new election to fill the office

sources.quote: When two or more candidates for the same office, after a full recount of votes, have an equal and the highest number of votes: [...] (2) For election to a public office other than Governor or those referred to in subsection (1) of this section, the Secretary of State by proclamation shall order a new election to fill the office.

ties.note: The text says 'a public office other than Governor or those referred to in subsection (1)'; it names no federal office. U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, presidential electors and statewide offices are read as such offices because they are neither the Governor nor offices with a non-State elections officer or state legislators [inferred]. The date of the new election is not stated in this section.

ties.applies_to: election to Governor, after a full recount (ORS 254.575(3))
ties.steps: a full recount is made first; if the candidates are still tied the Legislative Assembly, at the beginning of the next regular session, meets jointly and elects one of the candidates

sources.quote: When two or more candidates for the same office, after a full recount of votes, have an equal and the highest number of votes: [...] (3) For election to Governor, the Legislative Assembly at the beginning of the next regular session shall meet jointly and elect one of the candidates.

ties.applies_to: nomination by one major political party to an office, after a full recount (ORS 254.575(4))
ties.steps: a full recount is made first (automatic on a tie); if the candidates are still tied the elections officer who receives filings for nomination to the office has them meet publicly to decide by lot who is nominated
ties.who: the elections officer who receives the filings for nomination to the office

sources.quote: When two or more candidates for the same office, after a full recount of votes, have an equal and the highest number of votes: [...] (4) For nomination by one major political party to an office, the elections officer who receives filings for nomination to the office shall have the candidates meet publicly to decide by lot who is nominated.

ties.note: Only 'one major political party' nominations are covered by this subsection; a tie in a minor-party nomination or for a place at a nonpartisan election (ORS 249.088) is not covered by the sections read.

ties.steps: no provision found saying what a tie vote on a measure does
ties.note: ORS 254.575 and the recount chapter 258 (sections 258.006 to 258.300) were read; ORS 254.575 speaks of 'candidates for the same office' only. ORS 258.290 requires a full recount of a measure when the difference is not more than one-fifth of one percent, which includes a tie, but says nothing of the result of a tie. An absence cannot be confirmed from these two chapters alone.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes for both candidates (the apparently elected candidate and the closest apparently defeated opponent)
threshold.conditions: the canvass reveals either that two or more candidates have an equal and the highest number of votes, or that the difference is not more than one-fifth of one percent
threshold.in_words: a tie, or a difference between the apparent winner and the closest apparently defeated opponent of not more than one-fifth of one percent of the total votes for both candidates

recounts.cost_bearer: the county for a county office, the city for a city office, the special district for a special district office, the state for any other office

sources.quote: The Secretary of State shall order a full recount of the votes cast for nomination or election to a public office for which the Secretary of State is the filing officer, and the county clerk who conducted the election shall order a full recount of the votes cast for nomination or election to any other public office if the canvass of votes of the election reveals that:

The difference in the number of votes cast for a candidate apparently nominated or elected to the office and the votes cast for the closest apparently defeated opponent is not more than one-fifth of one percent of the total votes for both candidates.

The cost of a full recount conducted under this section shall be paid by the county for a county office, by the city for a city office, by the special district for a special district office or by the state for any other office.

recounts.note: 'Public office' and 'nomination' are not limited by kind in the text; the kinds list is a mapping [inferred]. Both triggers lead to a full recount ordered by the Secretary of State (offices it takes filings for) or the county clerk. The 'votes: 0' field records the tie alternative.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for the office
threshold.conditions: the number of votes cast for a candidate differs from a majority of votes cast for the office by not more than one-fifth of one percent; unless otherwise provided by a home rule charter; does not apply to the office of sheriff, county clerk, county treasurer or a candidate to fill a vacancy under ORS 249.091
threshold.in_words: a candidate's vote total within one-fifth of one percent of the total votes cast for the office of a majority (the threshold for winning outright at a nonpartisan election)

recounts.cost_bearer: the county, city, special district or the state, as for the preceding rule

sources.quote: Unless otherwise provided by a home rule charter, at an election described in ORS 249.088, the Secretary of State shall order a full recount of the votes cast for nomination or election to a nonpartisan office for which the Secretary of State is the filing officer, and the county clerk who conducted the election shall order a full recount of the votes cast for nomination or election to any other nonpartisan office, if the canvass of votes of the election reveals that the number of votes cast for a candidate differs from a majority of votes cast for the office by not more than one-fifth of one percent of the total votes cast for the office.

recounts.note: ORS 249.088 (which election it describes, and what happens when no candidate has a majority) was not read; the kinds are a mapping of 'nonpartisan office' to judicial and local offices [inferred].

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for and against the measure
threshold.conditions: does not apply to an election at which at least 50 percent of registered voters must cast a ballot under sections 11 and 11k, Article XI, Oregon Constitution, if fewer than 50 percent cast ballots
threshold.in_words: a difference between votes for and votes against of not more than one-fifth of one percent of the total votes cast for and against the measure

recounts.cost_bearer: the state, county, city or special district for which the measure was proposed

sources.quote: If the official canvass of votes of an election reveals that the difference in the number of votes cast for or against any measure is not more than one-fifth of one percent of the total votes cast for and against the measure, the Secretary of State, in the case of a measure for which the Secretary of State is the filing officer, and the county clerk who conducted the election in the case of any other measure shall order a full recount of all votes cast for the measure.
The cost of a full recount conducted under this section shall be paid by the state, county, city or special district for which the measure was proposed.

threshold.conditions: filed with the Secretary of State not later than the 42nd day after the election (first demand) and the 52nd day (supplemental demand)
threshold.in_words: no margin condition: a candidate, or a political party officer on behalf of a candidate, may demand a partial or full recount

who_may_request: an officer of a political party on behalf of a candidate of the party
a county clerk (no deposit; the county pays)
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by a cash deposit of $15 per precinct to be recounted, up to $8,000 for all precincts in the state; refunded if the full recount shows a candidate for whose benefit it was demanded received a plurality; the requester pays any cost over the deposit when not refunded; a county clerk's demand is paid by the county
recounts.waiver: the Secretary of State may waive the deposit on a county clerk's application if, after the first demand, it appears that a nondeliberate and material error by a local elections official or the county clerk will change the outcome; that county then pays

sources.quote: A candidate or an officer of a political party on behalf of a candidate of the political party may file a demand requiring the Secretary of State to direct that a recount be made in specified precincts in which votes were cast for the nomination or office for which the candidate received a vote.

each demand shall be accompanied by a cash deposit of $15 for each precinct to be recounted up to a maximum of $8,000 for a recount of all precincts in the state on a measure or for a nomination or office.

If the abstract of votes resulting from a full recount shows that the outcome of the election on the measure was changed or that a candidate for whose benefit the recount was demanded received a plurality of the votes, the deposit required by ORS 258.161 shall be refunded by the Secretary of State to the person who filed the demand.

recounts.note: A partial recount does not change the official returns: the person demanding is bound by the original returns unless a full recount is demanded (ORS 258.171, not quoted). Only one recount is made per office (ORS 258.181, not quoted). Kinds are a mapping of 'nomination or office' [inferred].

threshold.conditions: full recount only; filed no later than five business days after the Secretary of State declares the result under ORS 254.555
threshold.in_words: no margin condition: a demand made on behalf of the electors of presidential and vice presidential candidates is for a full recount only

who_may_request: a candidate or an officer of a political party on behalf of a candidate (the general demand of ORS 258.161(1) read for the presidential electors' candidates)
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by the deposit and excess-cost rules of ORS 258.161(5) and 258.250 (a full recount of all precincts in the state: up to $8,000 deposit)

sources.quote: A demand for a recount made under this section on behalf of the electors of presidential and vice presidential candidates shall be for a full recount only and shall be filed no later than five business days after the Secretary of State declares the result of the election under ORS 254.555.

threshold.conditions: filed with the Secretary of State not later than the 42nd day after the election (first demand)
threshold.in_words: no margin condition: any elector may demand a recount of a measure

who_may_request: a county clerk (no deposit; the county pays)
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by a cash deposit of $15 per precinct, up to $8,000; refunded if the full recount changes the outcome of the measure
recounts.waiver: as for candidate recounts: on a county clerk's application if a nondeliberate and material local error will change the outcome

sources.quote: An elector may file a demand requiring the Secretary of State to direct that a recount be made in specified precincts in which votes were cast on any measure which appeared on the ballot.

unread.what: ORS 249.088 and 249.091 (nonpartisan elections, vacancies), city and county charters, and the Oregon Constitution
unread.reason: not part of chapters 254 and 258 as read; local charters were not read (state general law only)

notes: Pages were fetched once each from oregonlegislature.gov on 2026-11-07. The pages carry a few non-UTF-8 bytes (section signs and apostrophes) that the helper shows as replacement characters; the quotations avoid them.
Chapter 254 was searched for tie, by lot and equal number of votes; ORS 254.575 is the only tie provision found. Chapter 258 was read through (recount sections 258.150 to 258.300).

In Oregon a tie always triggers a full recount first (ORS 258.280(1)(a)); only if it persists does the lot (legislature, local, primary), a new election (federal, statewide other than governor, presidential electors) or the Legislative Assembly (governor) apply.
